question: How long does each of the desk's two advisory readers take to read a diff of about 5,000, 25,000 and 60,000 characters (60,000 is the Kernel's bound) at the efforts the configuration gives it, Astra at xhigh and at max and Kimi at xhigh, and does any read meet its configured output cap?
pass: Written before the run, in issue 1068 at 2026-11-21T00:36Z, nothing having run (trial TA3 of decision 0224's plan). The plan's row says twelve reads but names three readings of three sizes, two each, and five of six at max: eighteen were run, six of Astra at xhigh, six at max, six of Kimi at xhigh, three at once, one for each reading. The requests left the desk, not a GitHub runner, with the desk resource's own key read in-process and never printed, logged or written (the Builder's ruling (a)); the times are the desk's. The code is the build's own at harness/advise-deletes-each-response-390 3764aa12 (harness.advise.prompt_of and one, adapters/azure.Live, adapters/advice.read), each reader's settings from its config/harness.json (output caps 96,000 and 40,000 tokens), the effort set by the trial, each read given the step's 1,080 s and judged against its 540 s share, each stored response deleted once read. The diffs: from canary main e9a2da21 to trial/p-78-5k 13206558, trial/p-78-25k 81dea5a6 and trial/p-78-60k ef8649f0, each adding one file of the Factory's repo at ef796789: adapters/edits.py, tools/check_decisions.py, tools/check_trials.py, 5,185, 23,872 and 58,614 characters as a diff. Pass: every xhigh read, Astra's and Kimi's, ends within 540 s of its first request; at max, at least five of Astra's six do; no read ends incomplete, cut_short. One exchange is kept for each read, its times and counts in the call: Kimi's answer, and Astra's delete, the read's status, usage and finding count in the call. Result: fail, on two points. Every xhigh read ended within 540 s: Astra 95 to 409 s (5k 191 and 95, 25k 283 and 302, 60k 378 and 409), Kimi 40 to 234 s. At max, two of six did: 490 and 357 s at 5k, then 697 and 686 s at 25k and 682 and 642 s at 60k, each writing 42,000 to 44,500 tokens out, under half its cap. One of Kimi's two reads of the 60k diff ended incomplete, cut_short, at its 40,000-token cap after 234 s; its other wrote 33,210, and its two of the 25k diff 33,337 and 35,288, so Kimi at xhigh runs near its cap on any diff past a few thousand characters. Every read completed but that one; every one of Astra's twelve responses was deleted, deleted true. Spent $20.03 at the configured prices, under twice the estimate of $12; Azure's own figure for the day is owed from the desk's read of the resource. What follows is proposed, not decided here: Kimi's output cap raised, or its effort lowered, on large diffs; max not used on critical paths within a 540 s share, or the shares or the step's limit changed.
